content:
lee: Heads up — we're designing the rollout for the new quota_override flag, and it depends on user_segment + billing_tier. Want to avoid a cascade of partial activations. Thoughts on activation waves?

tim: I think waves by percent are simplest, but dependency on billing_tier complicates it. If tier=b and percent=10% you might hit 0 users in that tier.

maria: Agreed. We should support combinatorial targeting: percent within segment. e.g. percent:10 for segment:enterprise. That way we can do per-segment waves.

sofia: UX note — console needs to show per-segment progress not global percent. Ops will ask "how many enterprise users have this flag".

aj: From runtime side, we need deterministic hashing to stable-split users. We currently use user_id % 100 for percent. That works per-segment if you apply segment filter first. But we must version the hash seed so rollout is reproducible across releases.

lee: Good point about seed. Also need safe rollback hooks: auto-revert if latency or error_rate spikes > 2x baseline for 5m. Can runtime expose metrics to the rollout controller?

tim: We can emit a rollout-lifecycle metric per flag: rollout.percent, rollout.segment, rollout.seed, rollout.phase. The controller can subscribe for aggregate anomalies.

maria: Example config (proposal):
```yaml
flag: quota_override
targets:
  - segment: enterprise
    percent: 10
  - segment: beta_users
    percent: 50
seed: 42
phases:
  - name: canary
    duration: 15m
    auto_revert: true
    revert_thresholds:
      error_rate_multiplier: 2.0
      p95_latency_ms_increase: 150
```

sofia: Love it. Console should show per-phase timeline + live metrics overlay (errors, p95). Maybe a subtle red/orange/green indicator.

aj: Runtime API considerations: PATCH /flags/:id/rollout should be idempotent and accept a phase token. Also we should gate server-side: only a single active rollout per flag. No overlapping partials.

lee: What about flag dependencies? If quota_override depends on quota_v2 being enabled, we must ensure activation order. Prefer allow-listing dependent flags in the spec and runtime enforces ordering.

tim: Two approaches: soft dependency (check at evaluation time) vs hard dependency (runtime refuses activation until dependency flagged active). Hard seems safer for safety-critical flags.

maria: Hard dependency requires us to define dependency graph and detect cycles. We should add a validator at config update time. Rejection with clear message if cycle detected.

sofia: UX again — when editing rollout we should surface dependency warnings inline, and show the required preconditions. Also allow a "simulate" button to preview evaluation sample.

aj: Telemetry gating: we should tag metrics with rollout.phase + rollout.seed so we can slice by phase. Also include config_version in metrics to correlate regressions.

lee: Operational playbook snippet:
- create rollout in staging with same seed
- smoke test with sample users
- promote to canary enterprise (10%)
- monitor 10m, if healthy move to 50%
- auto-revert on revert_thresholds

tim: Quick API debate: should the console change the seed on each manual re-roll? I say no — changing seed reassigns percent buckets which is surprising. Seed change should be explicit "re-assign buckets" action.

maria: Agreed. Default: seed stays fixed unless you click "reshuffle". Log the reshuffle as an event.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout quota_override -> canary (enterprise 10%) applied to prod at 2026-03-20T15:12:34Z

sofia: One more edge case — cohorts that are temporal (last-7-days-active). Percent hashing for temporal cohorts can be unstable. We should treat temporal segments as dynamic and prefer allowlists or deterministic bucketing based on persistent identifier.

aj: We'll add a lint rule: warn when percent targeting used with dynamic segments.

lee: Next steps: aj to draft runtime API changes + validator, maria to update config schema PR, sofia to wire console UX mockups, tim to add telemetry metric names. Sync tomorrow 11am.

maria: I'll also add an integration test that simulates seed collisions across rollouts.

tim: Also document rollback SLAs for sales/CS so they know expectations.

lee: Thanks team :thumbsup:
